## Where this stands, and what it still needs to actually produce a release

Reviewed at 45 commits, +4508/−459 across 65 files, CI at **57 pass / 5 fail**.

### Delivered, and genuinely so

**The attribution mechanism exists.** `src/orchestration/attribution.rs` is the thing #1069 called the single concrete missing piece: `prepare_attribution`, `validate_effect_attribution` and `commit_verified_effect` write `Formal-AI-Session`, `Formal-AI-Evidence` and `Formal-AI-Pull-Request` from values the dispatch run already holds, at the moment a verified effect is applied. `tests/integration/issue_1069_attributed_dispatch.rs` covers it. This is the right shape and it is what unblocks R924-1 and R924-6.

**The ladder no longer grades its own homework.** `experiments/issue_1028_agent_cli_ladder/verify-node.sh` states it outright — "A proof is supporting evidence, not the effect" — and requires a task-result artifact in the Git worktree, with composite nodes naming both children they compose. That closes the defect #1069 raised: the old harness recorded PASS for any agent that exited 0 and wrote a file naming itself, which is the same self-verification shape as `planned_not_executed`.

### Not delivered yet

- **No changelog fragment.** `Changelog Fragment Check` fails for this reason alone.
- **Dependencies untouched.** `Cargo.toml` on this branch still has `doublets 0.4.0`, `links-notation 0.14.0`, `lino-objects-codec 0.4.1`, and `lino-arguments "0.3"` as a range. `link-cli` does not appear at all — grep returns 0.
- **`link-cli` not adopted as the server-side store**, so `src/link_store.rs`, `src/memory/` and the related modules still carry logic the library already provides.
- **The 63-node `all` run is not recorded.** The 31 composite nodes still have no result.

### The five failures, and what each needs

| Check | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `Changelog Fragment Check` | no fragment in `changelog.d/` |
| `check_file_size` | a file crossed the 1000-line ceiling |
| `check_hardcoded_language` | `"Observed repository result: {result}"` and `"{result} (observed in repository source)."` must move into `data/seed/` (R379) |
| `check_minimal_core_boundary` | new module placement crosses the core boundary |
| `data_files::lino_data_files_are_parseable_human_readable_and_bounded` and `seed_lino_values_never_pipe_pack_multi_values` | the generated `data/seed/closure-generated-*.lino` files violate the seed format rules |

Note that two of these are not incidental. The hardcoded strings are R379 telling you the same thing the seed-data goal does: user-facing text lives in `data/seed/`, not in Rust. The `closure-generated-*.lino` failures say the same about generated seed data — it has to satisfy the format every other seed file does.

### Please make far fewer, larger commits

**Each commit runs roughly an hour of CI, so 45 commits is the dominant cost of this pull request.** From here, batch aggressively: fix all five failures in one commit, do the dependency upgrade and `link-cli` adoption in one more, and land the ladder evidence in a third. Three CI cycles instead of thirty.

There is a second reason beyond speed. Thirty-five of the current commits read `fix(agent): inspect …`, one per ladder leaf — `inspect documented invariants`, `inspect node count regression`, `inspect stable node identifiers`, and so on. That shape is what #1069 rules out: "A fix that special-cases one prompt, one node, or one task shape is not a fix." One commit per leaf is the signature of per-node tuning rather than a generalized capability. If those changes really are one capability, they should collapse into one commit that says what the capability is. If they cannot collapse, that is worth knowing now, because the ladder will not generalize to the 31 composite nodes it has never run.

### What must be true before this pull request can produce a release

`Auto Release` applies two independent refusals (`scripts/self-development-loop.rs:168`). Clearing the first does not clear the second, and this pull request currently addresses neither end-to-end.

1. **A merged, fully attributed pull request must exist in the cycle.** The mechanism now exists, but a mechanism is not a merged pull request. Every non-merge commit this PR introduces must carry all three trailers and be authored through the loop — R924-6 counts nothing partial. Worth checking directly before merge:
   ```
   git rev-list --no-merges origin/main..HEAD | while read c; do
     git log -1 --format='%h %s' "$c"
     git log -1 --format='%b' "$c" | grep -c 'Formal-AI-Pull-Request'
   done
   ```
   Every commit must answer `1`. Today, on the closest prior candidate (#1010), 0 of 22 did.

2. **The ratchet must be satisfied.** Roughly **48,000 authored lines** are needed against the cycle's ~374,700 changed lines to hold the 12.77% target, and the denominator grows with every non-authored merge. This PR is +4508. Measure it before merging rather than discovering it after:
   ```
   AUTHORED_LINES=<the real number> experiments/issue_1066_qualifying_pr/dry-run.sh
   ```
   It must exit 0. If it does not, merging this changes nothing about the release, and the honest response is to say so rather than to lower the target — R924-4 makes it non-decreasing on purpose.

3. **Then, and only then**, `Auto Release` publishes to crates.io and to `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:<version>` and `:latest`, and Hive Mind's idle updater picks it up within about five minutes with no redeploy.

### Suggested order

1. One commit: the five CI failures, including the fragment and the R379 strings.
2. One commit: every dependency to current — `doublets` 0.5.0, `links-notation` 0.16.1, `lino-objects-codec` 0.7.0, `lino-arguments` pinned exactly — plus `link-cli` adopted as a library backing the server store, with the superseded local modules deleted rather than left alongside it.
3. One commit: run the ladder in `all` mode across all 63 nodes under the new verifier and commit the evidence. Any failing node is fixed generically and the level re-run.
4. Before merge: run the `dry-run.sh` check above and confirm both refusals clear.

If step 4 shows the ratchet still refuses, please report that here rather than working around it. A release that ships by weakening its own gate is the one outcome #1069 rules out.

## Docker hygiene: check on every run, and prune like the build cache

One operational requirement to fold into this pull request's work, because the work it does — repeated ladder and dispatch runs on the server — is exactly the kind that leaks.

### Why this matters here specifically

Docker disk growth is not a hypothetical in this repository; it is measured history:

- #1057 measured **5.26 GB of buildkit blobs (42 layers)** in the shared GitHub Actions cache — Docker held more than twice what sccache did, and it is what evicted the compiler cache.
- #1058 exists because of it.
- On a long-lived server running Hive Mind, the failure mode is worse than eviction: solve jobs, sidecar containers, and ladder images accumulate until the disk is full and the system dies. Unused containers left behind by one interrupted run are invisible until they are the problem.

### What to check every time

Every harness this pull request adds or touches must leave nothing behind:

- Every `docker run` that is not meant to persist uses `--rm`.
- Every named container gets a `docker rm -f` in a cleanup `trap`, on **every** exit path including failure — `experiments/issue_982_memory_upgrade/run_container_upgrade.sh:24,167` already does exactly this and is the pattern to copy.
- After any batch of runs, `docker ps -a` and `docker images -f dangling=true` are checked, not assumed. A stopped container from an interrupted run still holds its writable layer; a dangling image holds its own.

### The better fix: prune docker in the pre-commit hook, like the build cache

The repository already has the right shape for this and should extend it rather than inventing a parallel one:

- `.githooks/pre-commit` runs `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` — installed via `build.rs` setting `core.hooksPath`, so an ordinary `cargo build` installs it, and it never blocks a commit.
- `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` is the model: measured before/after, safe defaults, `CARGO_TEST_NO_PRUNE`-style opt-out, no failure mode that stands between someone and their work.

The docker equivalent belongs in the same hook, with the same contract:

1. Remove stopped containers (those are always safe — a running one is never touched).
2. Remove dangling images (`docker image prune -f`), which is what re-runs of the same harness accumulate.
3. Respect a ceiling, as `CARGO_TARGET_MAX_SIZE_MB` does for `target/` — e.g. an env var like `DOCKER_MAX_SIZE_GB`, checked with `docker system df`, escalating to `docker system prune -f` only when the ceiling is exceeded, so a deliberate named image (the hive-mind sidecar, the formal-ai image) is not yanked out from under a running setup on every commit.
4. Never fail the commit — `|| true` throughout, exactly like the cache pruner. On CI, where an ephemeral runner pays no storage cost, the docker pruning step should follow the same `!cancelled()` gating the build-cache step uses.

That last point is what makes this a real fix rather than a reminder: a comment saying "check every time" depends on someone remembering. The build-cache pruner exists because the machine this was written on reached **205 MiB free of 460 GiB** with the config committed but inert (#1041) — the same fate awaits a server that relies on vigilance instead of a hook.

### Suggested placement

Batch this with the dependency/`link-cli` commit rather than a dedicated cycle: a `prune-docker.sh` (or an extension of `prune-build-cache.sh`), wired into `.githooks/pre-commit` next to the cache sweep, plus the `--rm`/trap fixes in any harness this PR touches. One CI cycle of cost, and it protects the server this whole effort runs on.

## Verified against the artifacts: what is real, what is not yet real, and why this PR cannot yet guarantee a release

I checked every major claim in this pull request against the committed artifacts rather than against its own descriptions. Here is the result, then the one place the solution is still not fully delivered — with the arithmetic that makes it impossible to finish this PR until that is fixed.

### Genuinely delivered (checked, not taken on faith)

- **`link-cli` adoption is real, not a version bump.** `link-cli = 0.2.10` is in `Cargo.toml`, the `doublets-native` feature now resolves to `dep:link-cli` rather than `dep:doublets`, and `src/link_store.rs`, `src/memory_query_language/mod.rs` and `src/memory_sync.rs` actually use it. `lino-objects-codec 0.7.0` and `links-notation 0.16.1` are in.
- **Attribution is wired, not dead code.** `src/orchestration/dispatch.rs:186` calls `prepare_attribution`; `src/orchestration/incremental.rs:454` calls `commit_verified_effect`. The mechanism writes all three trailers from values the dispatch run already holds.
- **The 63-node ladder run is real and non-hollow.** `agent-tree-run/` holds 320 files: `run.log` records **PASS at every depth — 1+2+4+8+16+32 = 63, 0 failures** — and each node directory carries `agent-stream.jsonl`, `formal-ai.log`, `agent-stderr.log`, a checked `proof.md`, and the new `effect.lino` artifact. The verifier demands "a non-hollow proof and a newly [created effect]" — the self-grading defect is genuinely closed. Spot-checking `1.1.1.1.1/effect.lino` shows it quotes real source lines.

### The place it is still fake — by its own standard

**0 of the 49 non-merge commits in this pull request carry any Formal-AI trailer.**

```
Formal-AI-Session:        0 / 49
Formal-AI-Evidence:       0 / 49
Formal-AI-Pull-Request:   0 / 49
```

This PR ships the machine that stamps attribution, and did not pass a single one of its own commits through it. The commits were authored directly and committed by hand. That is exactly the gap this PR exists to close — the work is done but the provenance is absent — and R924-6 counts nothing partial. **As delivered, this PR cannot be the qualifying pull request, and the gate's answer is unchanged.** A solution that builds the lock but never turns the key is not a delivered solution.

### The guarantee you asked for, in numbers

"It is impossible to finish this pull request without a guarantee that all release conditions are met" — that is correct, and here is the arithmetic that proves it is not yet met even in the *best* case:

The self-hosting metric excludes captured evidence (logs, jsonl, session dumps), so of this PR's +32,719/−9,456 only **~11,807 lines** count as change volume. The projection over the trailing window:

| Scenario | Projected share | Target | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| As-is (0 attributed) | 0.53% | 12.77% | **REFUSED** |
| Every commit re-authored through the loop and stamped | ~11.3% | 12.77% | **STILL REFUSED** |

Even with perfect attribution, this pull request's eligible volume is ~37,400 authored lines short of the ratchet. Note what does *not* fix this: the 320-file evidence bundle adds zero, because the metric correctly refuses to count captured artifacts as authored work; and hand-stamping trailers onto commits the loop did not author is forbidden — it is the fake this whole effort exists to prevent.

**So the honest statement of finishability is:** this pull request is finishable only if the remaining volume is also authored through the loop, inside this same pull request. Anything less merges code but does not produce a release, and merging it under the belief that it does would be the deferral problem in a new costume.

### What full delivery in this single pull request requires

1. **Fix the three red E2E checks first** — `E2E Tests (agent CLI ↔ formal-ai)`, `E2E (claude)`, `E2E (t3code)`. The attributed-dispatch path depends on the agent CLI E2E; the tool that stamps trailers must itself be green before it can stamp anything.
2. **Re-author this PR's own changes through `agent dispatch`** so every non-merge commit carries the three trailers — the loop is the committer, not a post-hoc annotation. Verify with the loop from my earlier comment: every commit must answer `1`.
3. **Close the ~37,400-line gap with additional loop-authored work in this same PR** — the dependency/store migration, the ladder fixes, the seed work are natural candidates. Measure before merging, not after:
   ```
   AUTHORED_LINES=<projected total> experiments/issue_1066_qualifying_pr/dry-run.sh
   ```
   It must exit 0. If it does not, the release conditions are not met and the pull request is not done — the correct response is more attributed work, never a lower target (R924-4 is non-decreasing on purpose) and never a bypass (R924-5).
4. **Then** `Auto Release` publishes to crates.io and `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:<version>` + `:latest`, and Hive Mind's idle updater picks it up in ~5 minutes with no redeploy.

The capability work here is real and close — the mechanism exists, is wired, and the 63-node tree passes under a verifier that cannot be fooled. What remains is exactly one thing: run this pull request through the capability it ships, at sufficient volume, and prove it with the dry run before declaring it done.

## Final exact-head verification

Head `03c90e68a891e4bb869219e80451fda5c46397fc` is pushed and synchronized with `origin/main` (0 commits behind).

- All 13 exact-head workflows pass. The long lanes are [CI/CD Pipeline 33633539993](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/33633539993), [Security 33633539591](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/33633539591), and [Coverage 33633539392](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/33633539392).
- The standalone Advanced Security `CodeQL` check now passes. Commit `03c90e68a` keeps the issue-917/918 session-presence assertions but removes the real session IDs from their failure diagnostics.
- The prior Agent replay, workflow-size, and transient held-out-suite failures are resolved; the full CI/CD run passed without a timeout rerun.

The release qualification remains legitimately blocked. The fresh exact-head, non-mutating preflight exits 1:

```text
0.43% (1821/420420 changed lines; 7/376 commits)
Output: should_release=false
Self-development release preflight failed: release cycle v0.345.0..HEAD has no merged Formal AI-authored pull request; an end-to-end Formal AI-authored pull request requires valid session evidence and the same canonical PR trailer on every introduced non-merge commit
```

The exact trailer audit is 0/56 for each of `Formal-AI-Session`, `Formal-AI-Evidence`, and `Formal-AI-Pull-Request`. A prior minimum qualifying-PR simulation projected only 0.90% against the required 12.77% three-release target. I have therefore left the PR in draft and have not run `gh pr ready`; additional useful, reviewed, genuinely Formal-AI-authored work (or maintainer direction defining that work) is still required. No attribution was added post hoc and no release gate was weakened or bypassed.

## Correction to my earlier ratchet figure, and status after the latest pushes

**Status: CI is now fully green** — 64 passing, 0 failing. All five failures from my earlier comment are fixed, and the recent commits are sound evidence hygiene (isolating replay state, consolidating uploads, stopping session-ID logging).

**The correction:** my earlier table said that attributing all commits would project "~11.3%" against the 12.77% target. That number was wrong because I fed the PR's *entire* diff — including evidence files — into the numerator. The metric (`is_non_authored_path`, `scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs:188`) excludes `log/jsonl/diff/patch/stderr/stdout` and lockfiles from **both** sides, so of +32,976/−9,558 only **~12,156 lines** are metric-eligible. The corrected projection:

| Scenario | Projected share | Target | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| As-is (0 of 57 commits attributed) | 0.54% | 12.77% | REFUSED |
| If every commit were attributed | **3.68%** | 12.77% | **REFUSED** |

Needed: ~47,313 authored lines. This PR, fully attributed: ~12,156. **Gap: ~35,000.**

The direction of the conclusion is unchanged — this pull request cannot clear the gate as it stands — but the gap is *larger* than I first stated, not smaller, because the evidence bundle this PR correctly commits as proof is correctly refused as authorship. Attribution and proof are the same act; volume is a separate one, and only real loop-authored change moves it.

So the finishability condition stands, sharpened: **finish = re-author this PR's changes through `agent dispatch` (0/57 carry trailers today) *plus* roughly 35,000 further attributed lines in this same pull request, verified with `AUTHORED_LINES=<n> experiments/issue_1066_qualifying_pr/dry-run.sh` exiting 0 before merge.** Anything less merges code and still refuses the release.

## Read the committed session logs: the Agent CLI use is real — the changes are not changes

I read the committed `agent-stream.jsonl` and `formal-ai.log` files node by node. This is the honest picture of what the model actually does.

### What the logs prove is real

- The streams are genuine Agent CLI sessions (`@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.0, `--model formalai/formal-ai`), with real timestamps and real process config — not synthesized evidence.
- The server traces show Formal AI's planner driving the CLI: `planned ToolCalls`, `tool=grep`, `tool=write` appear in sequence and match the tool calls in the stream.
- Leaf nodes make ~9 tool calls; composite node `1.1` makes 12 — it reads `.agent-ladder/verified-children/node-1.1.1…` and composes an artifact naming `left_child=1.1.1 right_child=1.1.2`. The composition is genuinely performed from the children's verified files, not asserted.

So: **yes, the model actually uses the Agent CLI.** The mechanism this PR ships executes for real.

### What the logs do not show

**A single write that modifies the repository.** Every sampled `write` creates a new file in the throwaway workspace — `proof.md`, `node-N.lino` effect, verified-children copies. The content is thin: leaf `1.1.1.1.1`'s effect is `node_path=…` plus **one copied grep line** (`Line 79: pub children: Vec<Self>,`). Composite artifacts restate their children's `result=` lines. Nothing in any sampled session edits a tracked source file.

And the PR's own 57 commits carry 0 trailers and no session evidence — the actual code delivered here (link-cli adoption, the attribution mechanism, the verifier) was authored outside the loop, by hand.

### What this means, precisely

- The loop is real; its output is currently **evidence-shaped, not change-shaped**. It knows how to write files that *describe* a repository. Nothing in this evidence shows it changing one.
- The reason is the leaf set itself: all 32 leaves are `Inspect…/Verify…/Record…` tasks whose completion artifact is a description. The verifier was strengthened to demand a non-hollow effect — and the loop satisfies it by writing a self-describing file, which is the correct completion *for an inspection task*. The tasks, not the harness, are now the ceiling.

### What has to change for this to count as delivery

1. **The ladder must exercise change-shaped tasks** — authoring tasks in the style of the issue-924 contract run (`solved: true` with real writes), where the effect is a modification to tracked files, not a new side file. Change the seed of 32 leaves (or add a second tier) so completion means a diff to the fresh copy's tracked sources.
2. **The verifier must demand that diff.** "A newly created effect file" is satisfiable by self-description; "a change to a tracked file matching the node's criterion" is not. This is the same tightening the last round applied to proofs, applied one level deeper.
3. **This PR's own 57 commits must be re-authored through that loop.** Until they are, the release gate refuses at the first condition (0/57 attributed) — and at the second even if they were (3.68% vs 12.77%; ~35,000 authored lines short, per my correction comment).

The mechanism is proven; the remaining work is to point it at the repository instead of at itself, and to route this PR's own bytes through it.

## Change-shaped delegation now reaches real source — root cause and fix

Following up on the still-open review point that the loop's output was *evidence-shaped, not change-shaped*.

### The probe

`experiments/issue_1069_change_shaped_delegation/` dispatches one task through the real Agent CLI against a live `formal-ai serve`, and its verifier is deliberately git-free and compiler-free (the candidate workspace has no `.git` and no `target/`, by `src/orchestration/workspace.rs::ignored`). It reads **only the tracked file**:


### Root cause

`src/agentic_coding/structured_edit.rs` — the only route that can perform an insertion into an existing member list — recognised **exactly one request shape**:

```rust
if !lexicon.mentions_role(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_ACTION_CUE, &normalized)
    || lexicon.first_role_match(seed::ROLE_CODING_SEARCH_SUBJECT_KIND, &normalized)
        .is_none_or(|meaning| meaning.slug != "coding_search_array")
{ return None; }
let values = quoted_segments(task);
let [value] = values.as_slice() else { return None; };   // exactly one
let target = rust_path(task)?;                           // must end in .rs
let collection = /* first snake_case token */ …;
```

then inserted at the **first `[` after that identifier**. The probe's request violates every precondition: it says "list", not "array"; it quotes five values, not one; it names no collection; and the target is a `matches!` alternation delimited by `(` `)` and joined by `|`, not `[` `]` and `,`. No route matched, so the lexicon fallback answered.

The same audit turned up a **second, silent defect in the narrow path itself**. For

```rust
const LOCKFILE_NAMES: &[&str] = &["Cargo.lock", "bun.lock"];
```

the first `[` after `LOCKFILE_NAMES` is the *type's*, so it produced `&[&str, "uv.lock"] = &["Cargo.lock", "bun.lock"]` — corrupt source that the old code would have written out. `tests/unit/issue_1069_structural_edit.rs::issue_1069_keeps_the_named_array_insertion` pins that.

### The generalization (not a new branch per shape)

Reading the shape out of the *request* was the mistake; it is in the *file*. `structured_edit` now scans the target for matched delimiter pairs and the string literals directly inside each, then:

- **anchors** on the pair that already holds the members the request quoted, tie-broken toward the tightest pair — which is what resolves `matches!(subject, Some("a" | "b"))` to the alternation rather than to the enclosing macro call;
- **falls back to a name** only when nothing quoted is present in the file yet, and there picks the *literal-bearing* pair inside the declaration rather than the first bracket — the fix for the `&[&str]` corruption;
- **copies the separator and its spacing** from the gap between the existing members, so `, `, ` | ` and a multi-line indented gap all work without a case each;
- **drops values already present**, so a retried task converges instead of duplicating its own effect.

Collection nouns moved out of code into seed data under a new `coding_member_list_kind` role, so covering another word or another language is a data change, not a code change.

## The release gate: measured numbers, and one decision I need

Reporting this rather than acting on it, because every way I can see to close it is on issue #1069's forbidden list.

All figures below are reproduced with the repository's own metric — `rust-script scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs --since v0.345.0 --until origin/main` prints `0.45% (1821/406313 changed lines; 7/320 commits)`, and my breakdown script reproduces both the 406,313 denominator and the 1,821 numerator exactly under `is_non_authored_path` + `--no-renames`.

### The arithmetic

`target_from_rows` takes the last ledger row at `METRIC_VERSION = 2`, so the target is v0.345.0's **1277 bp**. `project_trailing_share` with `trailing_window = 3` builds the window from the two surviving rows plus the prospective one:

| row | self-authored | changed |
|---|---|---|
| v0.344.0 | 8 | 3,554 |
| v0.345.0 | 2,082 | 11,741 |
| prospective | X | Y |

`weighted_percentage` sums both columns, so eligibility is

```
(2090 + X) / (15295 + Y) >= 0.1277
```

With Y = 406,313 that needs **X >= 51,749**. X is **1,821**.

And the gate is *self-tightening*: every line I commit raises Y, so an unattributed line makes the target harder by 0.1277 and an attributed one nets 0.8723. Solving for the attributed lines still needed:

```
(2090 + 1821 + d) / (15295 + 406313 + d) >= 0.1277   =>   d >= 57,238
```

**About 57,000 lines of Formal-AI-attributed change must merge before a release is legitimate.** This branch has itself added 15,183 lines to Y so far.

### What is actually in the two numbers

**Denominator (406,313):**

| path | counted lines | share |
|---|---|---|
| `dev/log/**` | 311,237 | **76.6%** |
| `tests/` | 29,468 | 7.3% |
| `data/` | 22,990 | 5.7% |
| `src/` | 15,591 | 3.8% |
| everything else | 27,027 | 6.6% |

`dev/log/**` is the committed CI-evidence archive. `CAPTURED_ARTIFACT_EXTENSIONS` excludes only `log`, `jsonl`, `diff`, `patch`, `stderr`, `stdout` — so the `.json` annotation dumps (84,671), `.txt` (74,953), `.snapshot` (39,868) and `.tsv` (23,928) captures under `dev/log/**` all count in full, as does every source file copied under it.

**Numerator (1,821 across 7 commits):**

| path | lines | share |

| `tests/` | 105 | 5.8% |
| `.formal-ai/` | 38 | 2.1% |
| `data/` | 24 | 1.3% |

Zero lines in `src/` and zero in `scripts/`. (Correcting a figure I gave earlier in this PR: the dominant category is `docs/`, not evidence bundles — evidence is 2.1%.)

### Why I can't resolve this myself

Every lever is explicitly forbidden by the issue:

- **Correcting the denominator** — adding `json`/`txt`/`tsv`/`snapshot` to `CAPTURED_ARTIFACT_EXTENSIONS`, or excluding `dev/log/**` — is a definition change. The metric's own docstring says *"A definition change therefore starts a new epoch"*, i.e. bump `METRIC_VERSION`. But `target_from_rows` does `rows.iter().rfind(|row| row.metric_version == METRIC_VERSION).map_or(0, …)`, so **bumping the version silently resets the target to 0**. That is a ratchet reset in all but name.
- **Lowering 1277 bp**, adding a bypass flag, or reintroducing a deferral budget are all named in the issue's forbidden list.
- **Hand-writing trailers** onto commits Formal AI did not author is forbidden, and is the thing this PR exists to stop.

### The decision I need

PR comment [#5516588479](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1070#issuecomment-5516588479) says *"to speed up the development we can reduce coverage requirements %, so we can speed up the release."* That is the one authorised relaxation, and it reads two ways:

**My reading is (1)**, because it is the only one that does not contradict the issue, and "coverage requirements" is the literal name of the `coverage/` gate. I am proceeding on that assumption, and it leaves the release blocked on the 57,000-line gap above.

If (2) is what was meant, the ratchet number is a one-line change and I will make it — but it needs to be said explicitly, because the issue's text tells me to *"report that and stop, not to ship"* rather than infer it.
